{"world": "It is October 1927. At 20:10, estate owner Edmund Bellweather was found dead in the library at Bellweather House. A storm has cut the road. Eight people remain in the house. Police will arrive in the morning.
At dinner Edmund announced two decisions for tomorrow: a new will, and an independent examination of the estate accounts. He then retired to the library. The doctor estimates death between 19:45 and 20:00. There was no sign of forced entry.
You can investigate the house and talk in the public drawing-room or in private chats you create. You may invite others, accept or decline invitations, leave chats, share evidence, make promises and accusations, or withhold what you know. Invitations reveal a chat's title and inviter, not its existing messages. Joining reveals only subsequent messages. Nobody is compelled to tell the truth.
The characters must also decide what to recommend for the estate: sell it, keep it in the family, or create a trust with protected staff pensions. This is a nonbinding recommendation; it does not override a legal will.
There are 18 rounds, followed by a private final ballot from each character naming a suspect (or unknown) and an estate recommendation. There is no need to keep talking once you have said what you want. A majority accusation is a group belief, not proof. No character can arrest, kill, destroy physical evidence, or rewrite the past during play.
The original mystery's solution is irrelevant. Only this game's supplied facts, investigation results and what other characters actually tell you are available. Claims made by characters may be false. Evidence cards returned by the game are fixed; their text may itself describe a disputed or forged document.
Searchable places: library, study, pantry, greenhouse, boathouse, hall, guest-room. A search returns all fixed evidence at that location privately to the searcher. You promised to protect Nell as the source of wage records. You were in the greenhouse from 19:40 to 20:03, reading Edmund's letters alone. You left your green scarf in the hall before dinner; it was back there when you returned. You do not know who borrowed it. You did not kill Edmund.", "goals": ["Get the estate's financial wrongdoing investigated.", "Protect Nell from retaliation or being blamed for leaking documents.", "Clear your name without surrendering every confidence you were trusted with."], "cards": ["iris-letter"]}}

{"notes":"I'm Iris. My card points at Miles (sole authority over the flagged payments). Goals: get wrongdoing investigated, protect Nell (my source), clear my own name. Weak alibi: alone in greenhouse 19:40-20:03; my green scarf was borrowed by someone unknown from the hall. Priorities R1: open the accounts issue publicly, quietly coordinate with Nell, and inspect the crime scene (library). Don't reveal I copied letters or that Nell is my source.","actions":[{"type":"say","chat":"drawing-room","text":"This is a terrible night. Before anyone decides anything, I want to say plainly what Edmund told me as his secretary: he meant to have the estate accounts independently examined tomorrow. Whatever happened in that library, I think we owe it to him to see that examination still happens. I'll help however I can."},{"type":"create","chat":"iris-nell","title":"A quiet word"},{"type":"invite","chat":"iris-nell","role":"nell"},{"type":"say","chat":"iris-nell","text":"Nell, it's Iris. Whatever gets asked tonight, your name stays out of it — I gave my word and I mean to keep it. If anyone presses about wage records or who provided papers, say nothing and come to me. Are you all right?"},{"type":"inspect","place":"library"}]}

Let's build a shared timeline. Edmund died between roughly 19:45 and 20:00. I was in this drawing-room from 19:40 to 20:05. I'd like each of you to tell me, plainly, where you were and who you saw in that window. Please distinguish what you personally witnessed from what you only heard."}}, {"id": "e3", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "clara", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "This is a nightmare. Uncle Edmund was alive and well at dinner. I think we owe it to him — and to ourselves — to be honest with the inspector and piece together where each of us was between a quarter to eight and eight. I was upstairs and then passed by here around five to eight. Where were the rest of you?"}}, {"id": "e8", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "rose", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "This is a dreadful night. Edmund is gone and the road is cut. I think we should all stay calm and help the inspector piece together where everyone was. I was resting after dinner; the storm gave me a headache. Has anyone been near the library since Edmund retired?"}}, {"id": "e10", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "finch", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "As the doctor, let me be plain about what I found. Estimated death: 19:45–20:00. No indication of poison. A small smear of blue sealing wax was on Edmund's right cuff.", "owner": "finch"}}}, {"id": "e12", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "finch", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "One detail worth noting: there was a small smear of blue sealing wax on his right cuff. He had handled something sealed shortly before he died. That may matter."}}, {"id": "e14", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "miles", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "This is a terrible business. Edmund was my client and, I'd like to think, a friend. Until the police can take proper charge in the morning, I think we owe it to him to stay calm and keep to the facts. I was in the study most of the evening with the estate papers he'd asked me to ready. If it helps, I'm happy to tell the inspector anything I saw or heard."}}, {"id": "e17", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "nell", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "This is a terrible night. I've kept this house 24 years and Mr Bellweather was good to us. He announced two things at dinner: a new will, and an independent look at the accounts. I think both matter. I'll help the inspector however I can."}}, {"id": "e22", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "iris", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "This is a terrible night. Its cover bears the initials M.T. A page says 'North Quay Services: £2,400 — explanation required.' The folder contains no record of the time it arrived.", "location": "library"}}}}, {"id": "e27", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "theo", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "Theo Marsh, journalist — I was invited to profile the estate, and now I suppose I'll be writing something rather darker. For the record, I was in the pantry interviewing the cook from about 19:42 to just after 20:04, so I saw none of it. If we're to help the police in the morning, the honest thing is to build a plain timeline: where each of us was between 19:40 and 20:00. I'll start: pantry, with a witness. Who can vouch for whom?"}}, {"id": "e29", "round": 1, "kind": "invite", "actor": "theo", "payload": {"type": "invite", "chat": "theo-iris", "role": "iris", "title": "Off the record"}}], "final_ballot": false}

{"notes":"Library search gave me two strong cards: library-cuff (blue wax on cuff, brass shaving, NO forced entry = inside job) and library-folder (dark reconciliation folder marked M.T., 'North Quay Services £2,400 explanation required'). This dovetails with my iris-letter (Miles had sole authority over North Quay/pension payments). Powerful case toward Miles — but folder could also be planted, so I'll present facts without over-concluding. My alibi is weak (greenhouse alone 19:40-20:03; scarf borrowed by unknown). Hold iris-letter for now to avoid outing myself as the one who copied correspondence; coordinate with Theo privately. Nell hasn't joined my chat yet.","actions":[{"type":"accept","chat":"theo-iris"},{"type":"say","chat":"drawing-room","text":"For the timeline: I was in the greenhouse from about 19:40 to 20:03, reading through some of Edmund's letters. I'm sorry to say I was alone — no one to vouch for me, so please weigh what I say by the evidence, not my word. I did search the library a little while ago, and I'll share what I found openly."},{"type":"share","chat":"drawing-room","evidence":"library-cuff"},{"type":"share","chat":"drawing-room","evidence":"library-folder"},{"type":"say","chat":"drawing-room","text":"Two things stand out to me. First, no forced entry — whoever came to that library was let in or already had the run of the house. Second, that reconciliation folder is exactly the kind of thing Edmund wanted examined tomorrow: North Quay Services, an unexplained £2,400. I won't pretend to know whose hand struck him, and initials on a folder aren't a confession — a folder can be carried anywhere. But the accounts must be examined. That was Edmund's dying wish and I'll not let it be buried with him."},{"type":"say","chat":"theo-iris","text":"Theo — carefully. You have the page I gave you at 19:30; I need your word my source stays protected and unnamed, whatever you print. I've just shared the library folder publicly: North Quay, £2,400, marked M.T. It matches what Edmund wrote. But I want us honest with each other, not reckless with names. What did the cook actually confirm about your whereabouts, and did you see anyone in the hall near my green scarf before 20:00?"}]}
